sections.title: Anchor the day to temperature minimum

items.q: How do you find your temperature minimum, and why does it matter?
items.a: Log wake time daily; lowest core temp ≈ **2 hours before** average wake. Best cognitive work lands **4–6 hours after** that trough, on the rising temperature slope (e.g. wake 8 AM → work bout ~**10–11 AM**).

**Optic-flow walk** outdoors (lowers amygdala activity) + **morning sunlight** for melanopsin/cortisol timing + hydrate with electrolytes. Delay caffeine **90–120 min** after waking to avoid afternoon adenosine crashes.

items.q: Why fast until noon and delay caffeine?
items.a: Fasting until ~noon raises **epinephrine** in the optimal focus band (not panic-jittery). Delayed caffeine preserves a **consistent energy arc** instead of an early-afternoon crash.

items.q: What makes a 90-minute ultradian work tunnel?
items.a: One "holy" block: timer, **phone fully off**, low white noise, screen **at or above eye level**. Accept uneven focus inside the block; dopamine/norepinephrine payoff on exit. Realistic deep work totals ~**3 hours**/day.

items.q: How should exercise fit without wrecking the day?
items.a: Keep sessions **≤1 hour** with an **80/20** split — 80% sub-max, 20% to failure/lactate threshold. Alternate strength and endurance; supports BDNF without all-day cortisol elevation.

items.q: How should carbs be timed for focus vs sleep?
items.a: **Low starch at lunch** (starch → serotonin → sleepiness); **starches at dinner** for sleep transition. Large meal volume diverts blood from the brain regardless of macros. Aim **≥1000 mg EPA**/day for mood support.

items.q: Why get outdoor light around 4 PM?
items.a: **10–30 min** afternoon outdoor light (~4 PM) desensitizes the retina to disruptive evening/late-night light (**10 PM–4 AM**), protecting night sleep.

items.q: How does a hot bath help you cool down for sleep?
items.a: Hot bath/shower/sauna **paradoxically accelerates** post-exit cooling; then sleep in a **cool, dark room**. Cool AVA zones (palms, face, feet) to drop core temperature faster.

items.q: What optional supplements are in the Huberman sleep stack?
items.a: **Magnesium threonate or bisglycinate**, **apigenin**, and **theanine** — simple levers that work because they hitch to the **nervous system**, not because they're exotic.
